question.text: Tanjore Capital (corporate investor in a Cat I AIF) earns exempt buyback income of INR 5 crore in FY24 (buyback on 20 September 2024 — before the 1 October 2024 cutover). Tanjore had booked INR 40 lakh of management-level expenses partially attributable to this exempt stream. From the LP's tax perspective, which provision disallows expenses attributable to exempt income?

answer.text: Section 14A read with Rule 8D — expenditure in relation to exempt income is not deductible

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Section 14A read with Rule 8D disallows expenditure incurred in relation to income not forming part of total income (exempt income). Buyback income pre-1-Oct-2024 was exempt under Section 10(34A); related expenses are disallowed under 14A. Rule 8D prescribes a formula for the disallowance. Post 1-Oct-2024, buyback income is taxable in the shareholder's hands (no 10(34A)), so 14A is no longer triggered for post-cutover buybacks. **The Trap:** Option A — 80M is the inter-corporate dividend deduction; opposite effect. Option C — applies to below-FMV receipts, not exempt income. Option D — treaty override is unrelated. **Cross-Exam Context:** XV and XXI-B test 14A/Rule 8D for listed portfolios; XIX-C tests it on AIF pass-through where some income heads may be exempt. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** For institutional LPs (corporates) running their own books, your Form 64C should segregate exempt vs taxable pass-through by head. The LP's CA uses this to compute 14A/Rule 8D disallowance accurately — saves the LP a scrutiny headache.
